result.title: PeekKV: The First Content Token Already Knows Which Heads Matter
result.summary: The size of the KV cache grows linearly with context length, making it a major memory bottleneck in LLM serving. Motivated by recent progress in identifying the functional roles of attention heads, a growing body of work compresses the KV cache non-uniformly across heads. Existing methods either fix the important heads via offline profiling or select them using attention signals from the prefill stage. In both cases, however, accuracy fluctuates substantially across workloads. While investigating the cause of this instability, we find that the active heads shift between the prefill and decode stages even within a single input. Along the decode path, by contrast, the activehead composition remains stable across content tokens once format tokens are filtered out. Based on this observation, we propose PeekKV. PeekKV observes a single content token immediately after prefill - a one-token peek - to jointly obtain head-group scores and token-importance scores. Guided by these scores, PeekKV allocates KV cache budgets to head groups in proportion to their group scores and retains only the top-scoring tokens within each budget. PeekKV requires no offline profiling or training and thus applies directly to unseen workloads and new models. Across four public benchmarks, PeekKV achieves the highest accuracy in more than half of the per-model comparisons against state-of-the-art methods, and stays closest to the full-cache accuracy on RULER and LongBench. On Llama-3.1-8B-Instruct, PeekKV retains 95.7% of the full-cache accuracy at a 10% memory budget on RULER with 16K contexts and 95.9% at a 1.5% budget on LongBench.

AI.brief_summary: 论文提出 PeekKV，一种无需训练与离线剖析的 KV cache 压缩方法：在 prefill 后仅「偷看」单个内容 token，同时得到注意力头分组分数与 token 重要性分数，据此为各头组按比例分配缓存预算，并在各组内只保留最高分 token。
AI.relevance_reason: 其关于活跃注意力头组成在 prefill 与 decode 之间变化、却在内容 token 间保持稳定的观察，可能为 LVR 中「注意力结构与缓存如何影响 latent 状态及相似度」提供核查线索；但论文面向纯文本服务效率，未涉及多模态推理，迁移需自行判断。
